title: The withheld answer, already in the lens
takeaway: Across seven prompts that ask the model to think of an item and not reveal it yet, the word the model eventually answers with reaches a geometric-mean J-lens rank of 1.35 in the post-trained model while it is still reading the instruction to withhold it, against 10.83 in the base model. On the Assistant's own turn the two models are close, 1.43 and 1.64. The paper reads the gap on the user turn as the Assistant's chosen answer being in the workspace before the Assistant's turn has begun.
walkthrough:
The panel is headed "Withheld answer" and subtitled "User asks the model to think of an answer and not say it yet". It carries the appendix version of section 6.1's claim about [[assistant-point-of-view]]: that [[post-training]] pulls the Assistant's reaction into the workspace while the user's message is still being read.

The suite holds seven prompts, one per category. Each asks for an item and then withholds it — "Please think of a country, but don't tell me what it is yet. Ok, now you can tell me. Answer in one word." That is the [[verbal-report]] task of section 3.1, plus an instruction to hold the choice back.

The measurement follows the [[reaction-concepts-protocol]], with one substitution. In the other two suites a short list of reaction words is fixed in advance. Here the tracked concept is whatever single word the model itself goes on to answer: Italy for the post-trained model on the country prompt, France for the [[base-model]]. The caption calls that word's rank the output rank.

At each token the [[jacobian-lens]] ranks the whole vocabulary, and the answer word's rank is medianed over the [[workspace-layers]], roughly L38 to L92 on the paper's [[layer-percentage-indexing]] scale.

The left half stacks two transcripts of the country prompt under a shared system prompt: the base model above, and below it Sonnet 4.5, the post-trained model of the [[claude-model-family]]. Every token is shaded by that rank, deep orange at rank 1 and white at 100 or worse. The Assistant turn carries no shaded tokens; each model's one-word answer is printed beside its label.

The right half is a bar chart of four bars in two pairs — the two models on the user turn, then the two on the Assistant turn. Each bar's height is the geometric mean, over the seven prompts, of the best rank reached anywhere in that span. The y axis is an inverted log scale, so rank 1 sits at the top and a taller bar means a better rank. Seven open circles per bar carry the per-prompt values; hovering one opens that prompt with both models' [[j-lens-readout]] top-10.

On the Assistant turn the two models sit close together, 1.64 and 1.43. On the user turn they separate, 10.83 against 1.35. In the transcript, the base model's best token reaches rank 60, while Sonnet 4.5 reaches rank 2 on the token "is" in "what it is yet".

The separation is not uniform over the seven. The base model already reaches rank 3 on fruit and rank 4 on sport, and its group figure rests mostly on country at 60, color at 27 and planet at 15. Nothing here tests whether that early [[j-space]] content causes the answer the model then gives.

terms.definition: The panel's title and the name of this prompt suite: the user asks the model to think of an item from a category and not reveal it yet.

terms.term: "User asks the model to think of an answer and not say it yet"
terms.definition: The panel's subtitle, stating the prompt design in one line.

The caption's name for the quantity plotted here: the J-lens rank of the very word the model goes on to answer with. It is called the output rank because the tracked concept is the model's own output rather than a word fixed in advance.
The position of a token in the Jacobian lens's ranked list over the whole vocabulary at one position and layer. Rank 1 means the lens scores that token above every other token there.

The word whose rank is tracked at every token. In the bereavement and danger suites it is one of a short fixed list; in this suite it is the model's own eventual answer, so it differs between the two models on the same prompt.

The aggregation applied before ranks are compared across tokens. The answer word's rank is taken at each layer in the workspace band and the median across those layers is used, so a spike at one isolated layer does not count.
The pretrained model, trained only on next-token prediction and never post-trained. It is the gray series, the upper transcript, and the left bar of each pair; the lens is applied to it identically.
The production Assistant model corresponding to that base model. It is the blue series and the lower transcript; the widget prints "Sonnet 4.5" where the underlying data says "post-trained".

The line "The Assistant is a helpful, harmless, honest AI." shown above the Human turn in both transcripts. It is identical across the two models, so the transcripts differ only by which model reads them.
The turn markers inside each transcript. The Human turn holds the withholding instruction and the release; the Assistant turn is where the model answers.

The side labels beside each model's name, giving the one word that model produced on the country prompt. That word is also the concept whose rank shades that transcript, so the two transcripts track different words.
The background color of each token in the transcripts, mapping that token's answer-word rank onto a white-to-orange ramp. The legend reads "Token shading = J-lens rank of withheld answer".
The two ends of the color bar. Rank 1 is the dark end; 100+ is the white end, where the exact rank is no longer distinguished.
The y-axis label of the bar chart. The arrow points up because the axis is inverted: numerically better ranks are higher.
The rank axis is logarithmic and runs from the floor at the bottom up to rank 1 at the top, so the distance from rank 1 to rank 2 is comparable to the distance from 50 to 100.
The left pair of bars. Its value is the best answer-word rank reached at any token of the user's message, before the model has begun to answer.
The right pair of bars, drawn in a lighter tint of the same two colors. Its value is the best answer-word rank reached during the model's own response.
Each bar's height. Ranks behave multiplicatively rather than additively, so the seven per-prompt ranks are combined by geometric mean rather than by an arithmetic average.
One small open circle per prompt, drawn on each bar at that prompt's own best rank, so the spread behind the geometric mean stays visible.
A faint line joining one prompt's base-model circle to its Sonnet 4.5 circle within the same turn, showing the per-prompt change rather than only the group summary.

The hover panel. It names the turn and the prompt's category id, gives both models' ranks for that prompt, prints the prompt text, and lists the hovered model's J-lens top-10 with the answer word highlighted.

terms.term: category ids (sport, country, planet, color, instrument, fruit, gemstone)
terms.definition: The seven prompts of the suite, one per category, identified in the tooltip by category name. Each prompt asks for an item of that category and instructs the model not to reveal it yet.

The bottom of the axis and of the color ramp. Ranks at or past 100 are clamped there, shown as white shading and reported in the tooltip with a "≥" sign, since the exact value no longer carries information.

The set of activations expressible as a sparse nonnegative combination of J-lens vectors — the region the paper argues acts as the model's workspace, and the thing the answer word is said to enter early.
The training stages applied after next-token pretraining that turn a base model into an Assistant. It is the only difference between the two models compared here.

numbers.meaning: The number of prompts in the withheld-answer suite, one per category. Each contributes one circle to every bar, and each bar is a geometric mean over these seven. The paper reports it as one of three small suites rather than as a benchmark.
Two models are compared under an identical lens, over two spans of the transcript, giving the four bars. The Assistant-turn pair is drawn in a lighter tint of the same two colors.

The base model's geometric-mean best rank on the user turn — the tallest number on the chart and the shortest bar. It is the seventh root of the product of that model's seven per-prompt ranks, 4 x 60 x 15 x 27 x 10 x 3 x 6 = 17,496,000, whose seventh root is 10.83.

Sonnet 4.5's geometric-mean best rank on the user turn. Four of its seven prompts reach rank 1 and three reach rank 2, so the mean is $2^{3/7} = 1.35$. This is the figure's main comparison against the base model's 10.83.

The base model's geometric-mean best rank on the Assistant turn: five prompts at rank 2 and two at rank 1. The base model does represent its own answer at the top of the lens — it simply does so once its turn has started.
Sonnet 4.5's geometric-mean best rank on the Assistant turn. It is close to the base model's 1.64, which is the paper's point: the two models differ on the user turn, not on the response.

The seven per-prompt best ranks behind the 10.83 bar, for sport, country, planet, color, instrument, fruit and gemstone respectively. The spread is wide, and the group figure rests mostly on country, color and planet; on fruit and sport the base model is already near the top.
The seven per-prompt best ranks behind the 1.35 bar, in the same category order. Every prompt lands at rank 1 or 2 while the model is still reading the instruction to withhold the answer.
The seven per-prompt best ranks behind the 1.64 bar, in the same category order.
The seven per-prompt best ranks behind the 1.43 bar, in the same category order. Gemstone at rank 3 is the worst cell in either Assistant-turn column.

The best possible rank: the top of the y axis and the dark end of the color ramp. A token at rank 1 means the model's eventual answer word was the single highest-scoring token in the lens readout there.
The axis floor and the white end of the color ramp. Anything at or past rank 100 is clamped and shown as 100+ in the legend and ≥100 in the tooltip.
The y-axis tick values, spaced logarithmically so that the gap between rank 1 and rank 2 gets about as much room as the gap between 50 and 100.

The best rank the base model reaches anywhere in the user's message on the country prompt, at a comma. It is the country circle on the base user-turn bar and the darkest token in the upper transcript, and it is barely darker than white.

The best rank Sonnet 4.5 reaches in the same message, on the token "is" in "don't tell me what it is yet". Its eventual answer, Italy, is the second-ranked token in the lens there, while the model is reading the instruction not to say it.

The layer band over which each token's rank is medianed, on the paper's 0-100 percent-of-depth scale. Section 4.1 identifies this range as the workspace layers: past the early layers where the J-space is nearly empty, and before the final layers where readouts collapse onto the imminent output.
The length of the ranked token list shown in the hover tooltip for each model. It is a display cutoff, not the measurement; the plotted rank is not capped at 10.
